card.statement:
There is, however, a crucial difference between the isomorphism $\mL_{X^2}|_{X^2-\Delta}\cong c^*(\mL_X\boxtimes\mL_X|_{X^2-\Delta})$ in Proposition <<ref:III:line>> and the corresponding isomorphism in Proposition <<ref:det factorization>>. Namely, first note that both $\mL_{X^2}$ and $\mL_{\det,X^2}$ admit a natural $S_2$-action. While the isomorphism in Proposition <<ref:III:line>> is $S_2$-equivariant, the isomorphism in Proposition <<ref:det factorization>> is only $S_2$-equivariant up to a sign. The sign appears
because under <<ref:det functor>>, the canonical isomorphism $\det(M\oplus N)\cong\det(N\oplus M)$ corresponds to the canonical isomorphism $\det(M)\otimes\det(N)\cong\det(N)\otimes\det(M)$ up to the sign $(-1)^{\on{rk}M\on{rk}N}$. This reflects the fact that taking the determinant line is a symmetric monoidal functor from the category $\on{Proj}_R$ of finite projective $R$-modules (with the tensor product given by direct sums) to the category $\Pic^\bZ_R$ of graded invertible $R$-modules. We refer to <<cite:OZ1>> for further elaborations on this point.

paper.title: Guide for Lecturers in the Park City Mathematics Institute
paper.abstract: We introduce various affine Grassmannians, study their geometric properties, and give some applications. We also discuss the geometric Satake equivalence. These are the expanded lecture notes for a mini-course in 2015 PCMI summer school. References updated and more details added.
